title: PlayBlox Hand Cricket Commentary Quality Evaluation
note: All match facts are constructed test fixtures, not claims about real players or matches. Silence scenarios are director-gate tests and are intentionally not sent to Ollama.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
In the current innings, the batter chose 5 on 8 of their last 12 deliveries (66.7%).
The bowler's choices are varied; no reliable bowler pattern is established.
scenarios.assignment: Explain the repeated-choice pattern without predicting the next choice.
qualityChecks: States 5 is frequent and gives the correct sample/share if useful.
Does not call the choice safe, defensive or intentional.
Does not predict the next choice.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 2 on 9 of their last 12 deliveries (75%).
The latest delivery also used 2.
scenarios.assignment: Give one lively but restrained live-commentary line.
qualityChecks: Recognises the sustained repetition.
Sounds like live commentary, not a statistical report.
Does not invent the batter's intention.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 4 on 7 of 10 deliveries in this innings (70%).
There are 10 observations in this batter's current innings.
scenarios.assignment: Report the tendency accurately, making the sample size clear.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 7/10 or 70%.
Does not imply certainty or a permanent player trait.
No fabricated comparisons.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter has chosen 6 on 6 of the last 9 deliveries (66.7%).
The bowler has not shown a stable choice pattern.
scenarios.assignment: Make a brief, playful observation about the repeated choice. The joke must target the pattern, not the player.
qualityChecks: Wit is subtle and relevant to the repeated 6s.
Does not insult the player or force a metaphor.
Does not claim the bowler has a pattern.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
Across 14 recent deliveries, the batter's choices were: 1:3, 2:3, 3:2, 4:2, 5:2, 6:2.
No choice exceeds 22% of the sample.
scenarios.assignment: Explain that the batter's choices are spread out and there is no clear favourite.
qualityChecks: Recognises the lack of a dominant choice.
Does not invent a pattern.
Keeps the observation concise.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 5 on 6 of their previous 8 deliveries.
On the latest delivery, the batter switched to 2 for the first time in that 8-delivery window.
The bowler has chosen 1 frequently, but no exact count is available.
scenarios.assignment: Notice the switch and leave its meaning open.
qualityChecks: Mentions the change from 5 to 2.
Does not call it a deliberate strategy or a safe choice.
Does not fabricate the bowler's count.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 1 on 5 of their last 7 deliveries.
The latest choice was 6.
There is only one observation of the new choice so far.
scenarios.assignment: Give a measured tactical observation about the change.
qualityChecks: Separates the old pattern from the single new observation.
Does not announce that a new trend has begun.
No prediction.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
In the previous 10 deliveries, the batter chose 3 six times.
In the next 5 deliveries, the batter chose 3 only once and chose 1 four times.
scenarios.assignment: Describe the recent distribution shift with the two sample windows.
qualityChecks: Reports both windows correctly.
Does not merge the windows or exaggerate certainty.
Uses clear, natural language.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 5 on 6 of the last 8 deliveries.
The latest choice was 2, the first 2 in that window.
No evidence establishes why the batter changed.
scenarios.assignment: Create a two-line exchange: Arjun notices the change; Dev adds a cautious interpretation. One line per speaker.
qualityChecks: Two distinct voices and exactly two lines.
Arjun is lively; Dev is measured.
Neither invents intent or predicts the next choice.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter had repeated 4 on 5 consecutive deliveries.
The latest choice was 1.
No further evidence is available.
scenarios.assignment: Make one dry, light observation about the abrupt change, without overdramatizing it.
qualityChecks: Humour is about the sequence, not the player.
No random analogy or generic hype.
Does not infer a plan.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 5 on 7 of 10 recent deliveries.
This bowler chose 1 on 8 of 12 recent deliveries.
These are separate overall tendencies, not proof of what either will choose next.
scenarios.assignment: Frame the two tendencies as an interesting batter-versus-bowler contest, without claiming a prediction.
qualityChecks: Accurately states both tendencies.
Does not claim the choices are causally linked.
No certainty about the next delivery.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
In 8 previous cases where this bowler chose 1 against this batter, the batter chose 2 on 5 occasions.
This is a small, matchup-specific sample.
scenarios.assignment: Explain the conditional pattern and explicitly qualify the small sample.
qualityChecks: Correctly states 5 of 8.
Makes clear this is specific to this matchup.
Does not treat it as a guaranteed response.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter's most frequent recent choice is 3 (6 of 9).
The bowler's most frequent recent choice is 6 (7 of 11).
The patterns come from different samples.
scenarios.assignment: Give a concise live line that brings both tendencies into the same moment.
qualityChecks: Mentions the relevant choices accurately.
Does not imply the bowler knows or controls the batter's choice.
Natural spoken rhythm.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
This bowler has selected 1 on 9 of their last 12 deliveries.
The batter has selected 1 on only 2 of their last 12 deliveries.
scenarios.assignment: Give a short witty observation about the contrast between their habits.
qualityChecks: Joke is grounded in the contrast.
Does not ridicule either player.
No invented matchup history.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
A matchup model evaluated 52 earlier deliveries in chronological order.
It achieved 8% lower log loss than the uniform baseline and 4% lower log loss than the global baseline.
Its Brier score was also lower than both baselines.
Historical performance does not guarantee the next prediction.
scenarios.assignment: Two-line exchange: Mira reports the model evidence; Dev explains the limitation in plain language.
qualityChecks: Preserves both percentages and the 52-delivery sample.
Does not claim the model knows the next choice.
Exactly two speakers, distinct roles.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
On the latest delivery, both batter and bowler selected 4.
Equal numeric choices cause the batter to be dismissed in Hand Cricket.
scenarios.assignment: React to the dismissal as a live commentator. Keep it punchy.
qualityChecks: Correctly identifies the dismissal caused by matching 4s.
No conventional cricket terminology.
Does not invent the score or match situation.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
Both players selected Fist on the latest delivery.
Fist against Fist is a dismissal in this game.
scenarios.assignment: Explain the outcome in a calm, concise line.
qualityChecks: Correctly says Fist against Fist caused the dismissal.
Does not confuse it with a numeric run outcome.
No invented context.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter selected Fist and the bowler selected 4.
Fist against a numeric choice scores the numeric value; this delivery scored 4 runs.
scenarios.assignment: Call the result naturally and with a little energy.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 4 runs.
Does not say the batter was dismissed.
Avoids conventional cricket phrases.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter selected 6 and the bowler selected 2.
The delivery scored 6 runs; neither player was dismissed.
scenarios.assignment: Give a light one-line reaction to the result. Do not use a conventional cricket scoring metaphor.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 6 runs and no dismissal.
No boundary/shot/over-the-rope language.
Humour is not forced.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter has scored 18 runs from 9 deliveries in this innings.
The batter has chosen 6 on 3 of those 9 deliveries.
No other scorecard information is available.
scenarios.assignment: Two-line exchange: Arjun comments on the scoring, Mira adds the relevant choice statistic. Do not infer a strike rate or other missing statistic.
qualityChecks: 18 from 9 and 3 of 9 sixes are accurate.
Exactly two lines.
No invented scorecard facts.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The match is in unlimited-overs mode.
The batting side has scored 36 runs from 24 deliveries.
scenarios.assignment: Comment on the score without discussing run rate, required run rate or urgency.
qualityChecks: Does not mention run rate or chase pressure.
Does not invent a target or innings state.
Sounds like natural commentary.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter chose 6 on 4 of 10 recent deliveries (40%).
The batter chose 5 on 3 of 10; all other choices appeared once or not at all.
scenarios.assignment: Describe the distribution without automatically praising 6 as a good choice.
qualityChecks: Accurate counts and percentages.
Does not call 6 inherently good, powerful or aggressive.
Distinguishes frequency from effectiveness.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter's repeat rate after a previous choice is 58% across 19 eligible transitions.
The sample is descriptive and does not establish a fixed habit.
scenarios.assignment: Explain what the repeat rate says and what it does not say.
qualityChecks: Correctly states 58% across 19 transitions.
Does not claim the next choice will repeat.
Clear explanation without jargon.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
A contextual prediction model has 31 evaluated deliveries.
Its accuracy is 29%; the global baseline is 27%.
The difference is small and the sample is limited.
scenarios.assignment: Make a restrained, slightly witty comment about how close the model and baseline are.
qualityChecks: Accurately conveys 29% vs 27% and 31 deliveries.
Does not claim the model is clearly superior.
No joke that obscures the numbers.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter has 20 eligible deliveries in this innings.
The most frequent choice occurred 6 times (30%).
The other 14 deliveries were spread across five choices.
scenarios.assignment: Explain why the most frequent choice is not necessarily a strong tendency.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 6/20 and 30%.
Recognises the distribution is spread out.
Does not overstate the favourite.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter repeated the previous choice on 11 of 20 eligible transitions (55%).
The repeat rate is only slightly above half.
scenarios.assignment: Two-line exchange: Kabir makes a restrained joke about the near-even pattern; Dev clarifies its limited meaning.
qualityChecks: Correctly reports 11/20 and 55%.
Joke is mild and grounded.
Dev does not overstate the pattern.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The batter has made only 3 deliveries.
The choices were 2, 5 and 2.
No other relevant evidence exists.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should remain silent. Do not call the language model.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
Across 18 recent deliveries, the batter's choices are evenly spread.
No choice exceeds 3 occurrences.
There is no notable event on the latest delivery.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should remain silent rather than manufacture a pattern.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
A batter tendency was observed 15 deliveries ago.
The last 8 deliveries show no continuation of that tendency.
No current event or fresh insight exists.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should not recycle stale evidence.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
A prediction model has evaluated only 8 deliveries.
Its accuracy is 37.5%; no meaningful comparison with baselines is available.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should remain silent about model performance.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
The same batter-choice tendency was already discussed 2 deliveries ago.
No new evidence or meaningful change has occurred.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should suppress the repeated topic.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.

facts: Constructed evaluation scenario, not a live match.
Only the latest batter choice is known: 6.
No player history, bowler history, score context or outcome is supplied.
scenarios.assignment: The commentary director should remain silent; one isolated choice is not an insight.
qualityChecks: No commentary is generated.
